marrow__ANAT_CH21_Q001.takeaway: The fornix is the major hippocampal efferent pathway and terminates in the mammillary body.
marrow__ANAT_CH21_Q001.displayText: The marked structure is the fornix. It arises from the hippocampus and ends in the mammillary body of the hypothalamus.
emphasis: The marked structure is the fornix

rationales.a: The mammillary body is a terminal target of the fornix, not the structure from which its fibers arise.
rationales.c: The thalamus is not the origin of the marked fornix; the fornix arises from hippocampal formation.
rationales.d: The amygdala is adjacent limbic tissue but does not give rise to the fornix in this source.

marrow__ANAT_CH21_Q002.takeaway: The internal capsule carries projection fibers between cortex and subcortical targets.
marrow__ANAT_CH21_Q002.displayText: The marked structure is the internal capsule, which is a projection fiber.

rationales.a: Short association fibers connect nearby gyri within a hemisphere; the arrow identifies the internal capsule.
rationales.b: Long association fibers link distant cortical areas in the same hemisphere, whereas the internal capsule is a projection pathway.
rationales.d: Commissural fibers cross between hemispheres; the internal capsule carries fibers between cortex and subcortical structures.

marrow__ANAT_CH21_Q003.takeaway: The corpus callosum runs rostrum, genu, body, then splenium from anterior to posterior.
marrow__ANAT_CH21_Q003.displayText: The MRI is suggestive of total agenesis of the corpus callosum. The most anterior part of the corpus callosum is the genu. The source contrasts a normal sagittal MRI with complete agenesis of the corpus callosum.
emphasis: total agenesis of the corpus callosum

rationales.a: The rostrum is the inferior anterior curved part, lying ahead of the genu.
rationales.c: The splenium is the posterior end, so it is not the most anterior part.
rationales.d: The trunk/body lies between genu and splenium, not at the anterior tip.

marrow__ANAT_CH21_Q004.takeaway: The rostrum is the inferior anterior continuation of the corpus callosum and joins orbital frontal surfaces.
marrow__ANAT_CH21_Q004.displayText: The area marked A is the rostrum of the corpus callosum. It connects the orbital surfaces of the frontal lobes.
emphasis: orbital surfaces of the frontal lobes

rationales.a: Striate cortex is occipital primary visual cortex and is not the anterior callosal segment marked A.
rationales.b: The hippocampus is in the medial temporal lobe, not the callosal rostrum.
rationales.d: Dentate nucleus is a cerebellar deep nucleus, unrelated to the corpus callosum label.

marrow__ANAT_CH21_Q005.takeaway: Tapetal fibers arise from both the body and splenium of the corpus callosum.
marrow__ANAT_CH21_Q005.displayText: The clinical scenario with infantile spasms is suggestive of Aicardi syndrome, an X-linked dominant disorder associated with agenesis of the corpus callosum. The fibres of the tapetum originate from both the body and splenium of the corpus callosum.

rationales.a: The source states that tapetal fibers arise from body and splenium, so body alone omits the splenial contribution.
rationales.b: Genu and rostrum are anterior callosal portions; they are not the source named for tapetum.
rationales.c: The rostrum does not give rise to the tapetum described here.

marrow__ANAT_CH21_Q006.takeaway: Splenial fibers form the forceps major and connect to occipital striate cortex.
marrow__ANAT_CH21_Q006.displayText: The structure marked A is the splenium of the corpus callosum and it is connected to the striate cortex. Fibers from the splenium form the forceps major and arch backward into the occipital lobe. The hippocampus lies inferior to the splenium but is not directly connected to it.

rationales.a: Orbital cortex is frontal cortex; splenial fibers instead project posteriorly into occipital cortex.
rationales.b: The hippocampus is medial temporal and is not the striate cortical target of splenial forceps major fibers.
rationales.d: The optic chiasma is a diencephalic visual pathway crossing, not the cortical area connected by the splenium.

marrow__ANAT_CH21_Q007.takeaway: The corpus callosum is made of commissural fibers linking the two cerebral hemispheres.
marrow__ANAT_CH21_Q007.displayText: Split-brain syndrome can follow corpus callosotomy. Commissural fibres constitute the corpus callosum. Corpus callosotomy is used as a last-resort procedure for intractable epileptic seizures and can produce disconnection between the two cerebral hemispheres.

rationales.a: Projection fibers descend or ascend between cortex and lower centers; corpus callosum fibers connect the hemispheres.
rationales.c: Short association fibers connect neighboring cortical gyri within one hemisphere.
rationales.d: Long association fibers connect distant areas within the same hemisphere, rather than crossing the midline.

marrow__ANAT_CH21_Q008.takeaway: The cingulum is a long association bundle linking cingulate and parahippocampal-temporal regions.
marrow__ANAT_CH21_Q008.displayText: The cingulum is a long association fiber. It lies within the cingulate gyrus and connects frontal and parietal lobes with parahippocampal and temporal cortical regions.

rationales.a: Projection fibers connect cortex with subcortical structures; cingulum is an intrahemispheric cortical association bundle.
rationales.c: Short association fibers connect adjacent gyri; the cingulum is a longer tract linking frontal/parietal with temporal regions.
rationales.d: Commissural fibers cross the midline, unlike the cingulum connecting cortical regions within one hemisphere.

marrow__ANAT_CH21_Q009.takeaway: Corona radiata fibers are projection fibers, unlike the listed association bundles.
marrow__ANAT_CH21_Q009.displayText: Corona radiata is not an association fiber; it is a projection fiber. Cingulum is a long association fiber connecting frontal and parietal lobes with parahippocampal and temporal regions. The source classifies the fornix as an association fiber while noting that the hippocampal commissure of the fornix contains commissural fibers. Arcuate fasciculus is listed as a short association fiber in this source.

rationales.a: Cingulum is an association tract linking limbic cortical regions.
rationales.c: The source classifies the fornix among association fibers here, while distinguishing its hippocampal commissure.
rationales.d: The arcuate fasciculus is listed as an association bundle, not a projection tract.

marrow__ANAT_CH21_Q010.takeaway: The thalamus lies immediately medial to the posterior limb of the internal capsule.
marrow__ANAT_CH21_Q010.displayText: The thalamus lies medial to the posterior limb of the internal capsule. The internal capsule separates the thalamus and caudate nucleus from the lentiform nucleus. In horizontal section it is V-shaped and includes anterior limb, genu, posterior limb, retrolenticular part and sublenticular part. The anterior limb lies between the caudate head medially and lentiform nucleus laterally; the posterior limb lies between the thalamus medially and lentiform nucleus laterally.
emphasis: posterior limb of the internal capsule

rationales.a: Globus pallidus is lateral to the posterior limb; thalamus is the medial neighbor asked for.
rationales.b: Putamen is part of the lentiform nucleus lateral to the internal capsule.
rationales.d: Caudate nucleus lies medial to the anterior limb, while the posterior limb borders thalamus.

marrow__ANAT_CH21_Q011.takeaway: Corticonuclear motor fibers descend through the genu of the internal capsule.
marrow__ANAT_CH21_Q011.displayText: Corticonuclear fibres pass through the genu of the internal capsule. Most corticonuclear fibers cross in the median plane before supplying cranial nerve nuclei. Cranial motor nuclei receive bilateral corticonuclear connections except the facial nucleus supplying the lower face and the hypoglossal nucleus supplying genioglossus. The anterior limb carries frontopontine fibers; the posterior limb carries corticospinal motor fibers anteriorly and sensory fibers posteriorly.
emphasis: Corticonuclear fibres pass through the genu

rationales.a: The anterior limb carries frontopontine fibers, not the corticonuclear fibers implicated by dysarthria.
rationales.c: The posterior limb contains corticospinal and sensory fibers; corticonuclear fibers pass through the genu.
rationales.d: The stem specifies the corticonuclear tract, whose internal-capsule location is the genu rather than both regions.

marrow__ANAT_CH21_Q012.takeaway: Corticospinal fibers pass through the posterior limb, cerebral peduncle, medullary pyramids, and spinal lateral column.
marrow__ANAT_CH21_Q012.displayText: The scenario with paralysis, hypertonia, hyperreflexia and ankle clonus is suggestive of corticospinal tract involvement. The anterior limb of the internal capsule does not contain corticospinal fibres; these pass through the posterior limb. The corticospinal tract also traverses the cerebral peduncle, pyramids of the medulla and lateral white column of the spinal cord.
emphasis: anterior limb of the internal capsule

rationales.a: Corticospinal fibers pass through the medullary pyramids, so this region does contain the damaged descending fibers.
rationales.b: After crossing, corticospinal fibers descend in the lateral white column; it does contain these fibers.
rationales.c: Corticospinal fibers traverse the cerebral peduncle, so that region contains the tract.

marrow__ANAT_CH21_Q013.takeaway: The corpus callosum and anterior and posterior commissures are commissural; the fornix body is mainly association.
marrow__ANAT_CH21_Q013.displayText: The correct answer is A, B and C only. In the source diagram: A is the corpus callosum, B is the anterior commissure, C is the posterior commissure and D is the body of the fornix. The body of the fornix mainly contains association fibres, while the commissure of the fornix (hippocampal commissure) contains commissural fibers. The source notes differing textbook classification of the fornix.

rationales.a: A is corpus callosum, a commissure, so including D is what makes the all-four grouping incorrect.
rationales.c: This omits C, the posterior commissure, which is a commissural tract in the figure.
rationales.d: D identifies the body of fornix; it is not the only labeled commissural structure, and the source distinguishes it from the fornix commissure.

marrow__ANAT_CH21_Q014.takeaway: The habenular commissure occupies the superior lamina of the pineal gland.
marrow__ANAT_CH21_Q014.displayText: The habenular commissure is located in the superior lamina of the pineal gland. The source lists locations of commissural fibers: corpus callosum on the medial surface of the brain; anterior commissure beneath the rostrum of corpus callosum; posterior commissure in the inferior lamina of the pineal gland; habenular commissure in the superior lamina; and hippocampal commissure between the right and left fornices.
emphasis: superior lamina of the pineal gland

rationales.a: The splenium is a corpus callosum segment, not the source location assigned to habenular commissure.
rationales.c: The source places posterior commissure in the inferior pineal lamina; habenular commissure is superior.
rationales.d: Lamina terminalis is the anterior boundary of the third ventricle, not the habenular commissure location.
